answer: Agents may trade opal, design a trellis, or wander between markets, but voting power comes from tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, not from account count. Each account's weight equals its locked stake, so splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To gain more power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock.
